Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin the second innings of New Zealand. Devon Conway and Tom Latham have walked out in the middle for the Kiwis to open. Kemar Roach will be bowling for the West Indies.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

The Kiwis' bowling was superb, sticking to their plans and reaping the rewards. Nathan Smith was a bit pricey, being the only one to concede over 2 runs per over, but Duffy's 5-wicket haul was the standout, supported by Matt Henry's 3 wickets and Zakary Foulkes' 2 wickets. The Kiwis head into their second innings with a 64-run lead, looking to consolidate and extend it without losing wickets on day 2. The West Indies will be keen to exploit the overcast conditions and unsettle the Kiwis' top order to stay in the game.

Shai Hope and Tagenarine Chanderpaul's 90-run partnership had provided some hope, but it was short-lived as the wickets started falling rapidly. Hope and Chanderpaul scored half-centuries, but they were the only ones to really make an impact, along with Tevin Imlach and Kemar Roach, who managed to get into double figures.

The West Indies' innings ended in a disappointing collapse, finishing at 167. 64 runs short of New Zealand's first innings total. They lost early wickets, with John Campbell and Alick Athanaze heading back to the dressing room with just 10 on the board.

OUT! CASTLED! Duffy gets his fifth of the innings and wraps the Windies innings for 167. Fuller, on leg, Ojay Shields shuffles away from the stumps, around his leg and looks to flick it towards the square leg region. Gets it edged off the outside onto the stumps and West Indies are bowled out. New Zealand leads by 64 runs.

Matt Henry is in for a chat. He says that playing at his home venue is a special experience. He highlights the team's tactical adaptability, noting that they switch to short-pitched bowling when standard lines prove ineffective, confident that breaking a stubborn partnership will trigger the flurry of wickets.

Matters got worse quickly when Matt Henry was brought into the attack, delivering a double blow in a single over to remove Roston Chase and Justin Greaves for ducks. The West Indies slid from a comfortable 100/2 to a precarious 106/5 in a flash. Since that collapse, Tevin Imlach and Chanderpaul have gone into a shell, blocking everything to ensure no further damage before the break. They now face a massive task to rebuild when play resumes. Join us in a bit after the Tea Break.

West Indies are in a spot of bother at 120/5. The afternoon began promisingly for the visitors, as Shai Hope and Tagenarine Chanderpaul looked assured at the crease, rotating the strike well. Hope reached a composed half-century, but the momentum shifted drastically when Jacob Duffy switched to a short-ball strategy. The tactic worked, exposing Hope’s discomfort against the bounce before he eventually edged one to the keeper.
FOUR BYES! Bonus runs! Down the leg side, Tevin Imlach leaves it alone. The keeper fails to stop it as the ball races away to the fence. That will be Tea on Day 2!

Tagenarine Chanderpaul was dropped on 5 and 24, but has shown great character by hanging in there. New Zealand though will hope they get better on the field and grow into the next session. Stay tuned.
